I should set vy to zero and verify the trajectory still passes near the rim center — at t=1.35 the ball's x and z put it just slightly past the rim threshold, within about 0.03 of the axis, which is close enough. Removing vy barely changes drag since vx stays the same, so the crossing point should hold up.

Checking clearances against both front and back rim posts as the ball descends, the distances stay above the required 0.127m margin throughout the pass, so it clears both the front rim at t≈1.28-1.31 and the back rim further along, before reaching the backboard face at 4.381.

After falling through, the ball's continued trajectory might eventually strike the support pole around x=5.1-5.3, but since the task only requires the ball to successfully drop through the hoop first, this later collision is acceptable. The ball also passes safely below the backboard's bottom edge at z=2.9 before any pole contact would occur.
